setting.placeName:
Vice-Consulate of the United States for the District of Lambayeque,
Chiclayo

opener.dateline:
Vice-Consulate of the United States for the District of Lambayeque,
Chiclayo, September 11, 1883.

div.p: Sir: Referring to my dispatch No. 131, of September 4, 1883, I to-day have the honor to communicate to you what since then has occurred in this district.

On the 5th September the Chilian war-ship Amazon arrived in the port of Eten, and immediately commenced to land troops. On the 6th, in the morning, about 150 men of the battalion Concepcion arrived in Chiclayo, and in the evening of the same day another force arrived, forming in all 600 to 700 men, with a few pieces of artillery. On the 8th the commander, Gonzales, called a meeting of the principal citizens and requested them to sign a document in favor of the cause of General Iglesias. Some of the gentlemen present expressed their opinion against this, and in consequence the whole meeting, composed of about seventy persons were placed under arrest, and ordered to pay fifty thousand soles silver ($50,000) and supply 100 saddled horses within forty-eight hours, in punishment for not signing the documents referred to. In case of non-compliance severe measures would be taken. What these measures are or will be I have been unable to ascertain, and only time will show. On Wednesday the term is up, and on Saturday next I shall communicate to you what may have happened till then. It is my opinion that the horses may be got together, but I think it utterly impossible to collect the $50,000 silver, principally as this department has already suffered so severely during former occupations.
During the absence of the Chilian forces, since the 26th July, the people of this town have behaved admirably, and have done everything not to compromise themselves.

The order was never disturbed, and when on the 28th of July the forces of General Iglesias arrived people quietly submitted to the new rule, so that the measures taken now by the Chilians appear to me to be very cruel.
